Class Spark

java.lang.Object
sootup.spark.Spark
public class Spark extends Object
Main access point to SPARK's functionality.

Exposes a PointsToAnalysis and the call graph it gives: built on-the-fly when SparkOptions#isOnFlyCallGraph() is set, otherwise the call graph the PAG is built on (CHA up-front, or supplied by the client) narrowed to the calls the points-to sets allow. Lower-level components such as the solver are package-private; clients should not bypass this facade. 

  Spark spark = Spark.builder()
      .view(view)
      .entryPoints(List.of(mainSig))
      .sparkOptions(SparkOptions.builder().onFlyCallGraph(true).build())
      .build();
  PointsToAnalysis pta = spark.getPointsToAnalysis();
  CallGraph cg = spark.getCallGraph();

To reuse a call graph the client already computed instead of having SPARK run CHA, pass it via callGraph(...). This is ignored (with a warning logged) when onFlyCallGraph is on, since OTF mode grows its own call graph incrementally from the entry points instead of consuming one.

Spark has no <clinit>-handling knob of its own; this is also the way to control it in the non-OTF path. Pre-build the graph with ClassHierarchyAnalysisAlgorithm's seedEntryPointClinits/sootup.callgraph.scope.VirtualCallResolver constructor and pass it via callGraph(...) instead of letting Spark run CHA with its defaults.

reflectionModel(...) (default ReflectionModel.none()) makes reflective calls explicit in every body Spark reads. dynamicInvokeResolver(...) (default DynamicInvokeResolver.bootstrapMethodHandles()) decides invokedynamic targets; values captured by a lambda flow into its body. When passing a pre-built callGraph, build it with the same model and resolver instances, else reflective/invokedynamic edges and PAG disagree.

implicitCallModel(...) (default ImplicitCallModel.threadStart()): calls that methods perform implicitly, e.g. Thread.start() calling run(), for OTF mode and Spark's own CHA. A pre-built callGraph brings its own implicit calls ( CallGraph.Call#implicitInvocation()). Either way, an implicit call is dispatched on the points-to set of its invocation's receiver, whose values flow into the callee, and attributed to the causing statement.

callResolver(...) (default DefaultCallResolver): the methods whose calls Spark's own CHA follows. Ignored with a pre-built callGraph or OTF mode.

  • Method Details

    • solve

      public void solve()
      Builds the pointer assignment graph and (in OTF mode) the call graph. Invoked automatically by the accessors; calling it explicitly is optional and idempotent.

    • getCallGraph

      public CallGraph getCallGraph()
      Returns the call graph that the points-to sets give. When SparkOptions#isOnFlyCallGraph() is set, it is grown on-the-fly during solve(). Otherwise it is the call graph the PAG was built on (the one passed to the builder, or one built via class-hierarchy analysis), without the virtual and interface calls that no object the receiver points to dispatches to, and without the methods that are then no longer reachable. The result is cached.

    • getPointsToAnalysis

      public PointsToAnalysis getPointsToAnalysis()
      Returns a points-to analysis over the solved PAG. The result is cached.

    • getPag

      public PAG getPag()
      Returns the underlying pointer assignment graph — intended for inspection and debugging.
